description: DRAFT provider-descriptor attempt for the ChatGPT subscription engine -- metadata, endpoints, the request-header template, and the named carve-outs. NOT the PluginProviderDescriptorV1 contract and not a frozen artifact; see docs/plans/plugin-chatgpt-descriptor-spike.md for the reasoning. The parts that describe SHIPPED behavior are executed below; the parts that argue about a future interpreter are declared non-executable.
notes: The header template is a pure name -> value map with two substitution points (a broker-held secret handle and an optional account id) and is asserted below against the real httpx client the engine builds. The descriptor bytes never carry a literal token: the runner substitutes ${ACCESS_TOKEN} with a synthetic value, exactly mirroring the production path where the token arrives via RuntimeConfig from Electron's initialize channel and is assembled into the headers dict by core sidecar code.

cases.rule: Pins the SYNTHETIC token the runner injects, so the header assertion below cannot pass by comparing two independently-drifting placeholders. No real credential appears in these bytes; that is what the redaction gate enforces.
Pins the synthetic account id used by the header cases below.
Pins the synthetic override base URL used by the endpoint cases below.

The OAuth client id is read out of services/backend/chatgpt-auth-service.js by the runner, so a rotation there fails this fixture instead of leaving the descriptor draft quietly stale. A public OAuth client identifier is not a secret -- it is published in the authorize URL of every PKCE flow.
Six headers, no more: the template is a NAME -> VALUE map with nothing else mixed in. Names are matched case-insensitively because httpx lowercases them on the wire.
ChatGPT-Account-ID is conditional: a blank account id omits the header entirely rather than sending an empty value, which the backend would reject.
One inference endpoint: POST {base_url}/responses with a server-sent-events response. There is no second call in the shipped path -- no model discovery, no capability probe.
The base URL is overridable but defaults to the first-party Codex backend; an empty or whitespace override falls back to the same default rather than producing a relative URL.

non_executable.reason: PLUG-D23 sequences the auth/network broker at Stage 5; this spike covers only the sidecar SSE-parsing/request-construction surface. The observed shape is: OAuth2 authorization-code + PKCE S256 against issuer https://auth.openai.com (/oauth/authorize, /oauth/token) with client_id ${OAUTH_CLIENT_ID}, scopes [openid, profile, email, offline_access], a loopback redirect on the first free port of a declared list, identity claims at $['https://api.openai.com/auth'].chatgpt_account_id / .chatgpt_plan_type and $.email OR $['https://api.openai.com/profile'].email, form-encoded body for the code exchange and JSON for refresh, permanent-failure codes {refresh_token_expired, refresh_token_reused, refresh_token_invalidated}, and freshness = now < jwt.exp*1000 - 5min skew with an 8-day fallback window from last_refresh_ms when exp is absent. Every field is already DATA in the current implementation, and the state-machine half (single-flight refresh, epoch-fenced sign-out race, JWT decode) reads as generic OAuth-broker machinery. It lives in Electron (services/backend/chatgpt-auth-service.js), not the sidecar, so nothing here can execute it -- only the client id is pinned, by the constant_identity case above.
A GET .../models discovery endpoint is planned but NOT implemented; there is no call to assert. See model_catalog.json's plan_vs_implementation_gap.

The two named carve-outs -- the citation-marker normalizer and the reasoning-item replay cache -- have their behavior asserted in streams/citation_markers.json and streams/tool_call_lifecycle.json. What lives here is the VERDICT that they cannot be expressed as descriptor data, which is a judgement about a hypothetical interpreter rather than an observable fact.

The claim that two-buffer terminal text resolution, call-pairing enforcement, placeholder suppression and the safe-scalar extractor belong in fixed provider-agnostic interpreter code rather than per-provider data is a scope decision about where future code should live. Each one's shipped behavior is asserted in its own fixture; only the disposition is unfalsifiable here.

The PLUG-D23 invariant is that provider credentials never reach plugin code and no secret_value_delivery grant is involved. There is no plugin code and no interpreter yet, so the invariant has nothing to hold over. Its two factual halves ARE mechanized elsewhere: the redaction gate in check_provider_descriptor_fixtures.py proves these bytes carry no credential, and the engine suite proves the shipped code keeps token-shaped text out of errors and logs.
